name: Learning and Training Methods
text:
# Learning and Training Methods
## Overview
This family encompasses optimization strategies for reconstructing 3D Gaussian primitives from 2D images, focusing on how the scene representation is learned and trained. It addresses the problem of parameter optimization (positions, covariances, opacities, colors) via differentiable rendering. It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Splatting Without the Blur](1157-splatting-without-the-blur.md) by its reliance on gradient-based learning rather than purely analytical or heuristic initialization, and from [Rendering Pipelines and Passes](1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md) by its focus on the [training loop](#4290-training-loop.md) rather than the inference rasterization.
## Shared principles
All methods in this family rely on differentiable rendering to compute gradients from the rendered image to the Gaussian parameters (position, covariance, opacity, [spherical harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)) and/or network weights [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, unofficial]. The rendering process remains differentiable with respect to the scene representation [S1, 6136-instantsplat.md, 6464-pixelsplat.md, unofficial]. Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].
## Subtopics

### [Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md)
[Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](#1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md) methods represent dynamic human subjects (typically heads or full bodies) as a set of [deformable 3D Gaussian](#10060-deformable-3d-gaussian-splatting.md) primitives driven by parametric models like FLAME or SMPL. Unlike static [Gaussian Splatting](946-gaussian-splatting.md) which assumes a rigid scene, this family solves the problem of rendering animatable, high-fidelity avatars from video by constraining Gaussian geometry to the parametric mesh surface and optimizing pose-dependent deformations. It differs from sibling methods like [Pose-free and Feed-forward Training](6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md) by explicitly relying on known or estimated camera poses and parametric priors for deformation, rather than learning [implicit mappings](#11979-imap.md) from unposed images. Specific to this family: Gaussian positions and orientations are initialized and constrained to the surface of a parametric mesh (e.g., FLAME for heads, SMPL for bodies). Gaussian parameters are functions of the parametric model's pose and shape parameters. This allows the avatar to be animated by changing the pose/shape inputs. Gaussians are typically initialized per triangle or vertex of the parametric mesh.

### [Pose-free and Feed-forward Training](6500-pose-free-and-feed-forward-training.md)
This family encompasses methods that reconstruct 3D Gaussian primitives from images without requiring pre-computed camera poses from Structure-from-Motion (SfM) pipelines like COLMAP. It solves the dependency on accurate initial pose estimation, enabling rapid reconstruction from casual, sparse, or uncalibrated image collections. It is distinguished from [Joint Pose Optimization](6888-joint-pose-optimization.md) by either eliminating pose variables entirely via feed-forward networks or fixing them during primary optimization, and from [Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction](1575-gaussian-avatar-reconstruction.md) by focusing on static scene geometry rather than articulated human models.

#### VS-Splat with GenDen Augmentation
[VS-Splat](#8542-vs-splat.md) integrated with the GenDen add-on model [S1, unofficial]. On CO3D dataset, VS-Splat + GenDen yields PSNR 22.09, SSIM 0.865, LPIPS 0.208 [S1, unofficial].
